newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB keeps Hungary 1997 GDP forecast at 3.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: CSFB keeps Hungary 1997 GDP forecast at 3.0 pct.

text.p: Hungary's 1.2 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the first quarter of 1997 was unsatisfactory, CS First Boston said in its weekly report, but added it left its 1997 growth forecast unchanged.

"First quarter GDP was somewhat disappointing, particularly after a recent three percent (annual) estimate give by Finance Minister (Peter) Medgyessy," said analyst Istvan Racz in CSFB's "Emerging Europe: weekly update."

Hungary's central statistical office (KSH) released its preliminary Q1 figures on July 1 and said GDP grew 1.2 percent in first quarter 1997 year-on-year, compared with zero GDP growth in the same period last year.
In fourth quarter 1996 Hungary's GDP grew three percent year-on-year.
CSFB said the slowdown was due mainly to a sharp fallback in inventory accumulation, which is likely to be a temporary phenomenon in the early stage of a recovery.
"For this reason, we are leaving our 1997 growth forecast unchanged at three percent," CSFB's Racz said.
